parent: main 74dd5d3 (V2-5 from PR #12; W=1024 / 256 threads retained by PR #13; full-collection baselines PR #16). main has since gained PR #17 (guarded FP32 baseline), which touches no file used here; the branch is not rebased so the variant commits stay fixed.
question: Do (1) a warp-cooperative block lookup, (2) a theta-filtered merge and (3) radix-select local top-k for large k reduce batch-1 latency of the range scorer, separately and combined, and where does the time go in ctrl and v3-all?
hypothesis: Each variant returns the canonical top-k for every calibration query. Speed effects are empirical; no speedup is promised. Laptop development readings suggested change 1 may be slower at k=10 (55 registers, 4 instead of 6 blocks per SM) and changes 2 and 3 faster at k >= 100.

v3-1.what: change 1: warp-cooperative block lookup (chunk 8 words, fix 1) and host thread-limit check

v3-3.what: changes 2 + 3: theta merge and radix-select local top-k (8-bit digits) for k >= crossover (15th scorer argument, default 100)

v3-all.what: changes 1 + 2 + 3 with fix 1 (lookup chunk 8, host thread-limit check)

selection_path_per_run: v3-3 and v3-all use the radix path at k >= 100 (default crossover). In the k=32 and k=64 sets v3-3 is run with crossover argument 1 so that it uses the radix path; v3-2 has no radix path. v3-all at k=10 uses the small-k path.

correctness_before_timing.gates: code/gate_build.sh for every build (ctrl, v3-1, v3-2, v3-3, v3-all, both clock builds, the stats build): tests/check_range_bitpack.py --encoding positions --single-kernel --max-k 1000 --v3-cases enforce (radix builds also with crossover 1, radix for every k); 100K and 1M x all 500 calibration queries x k=10/100/1000 against the cpu_pilot oracles; zero mismatches. Run IDs 20261117-cuda5-gate-<label>-01. The stats build (STATS=1) skips the fixtures, because each of its processes needs a new statistics file; it runs the 100K/1M x 500 x k=10/100/1000 oracle checks.
correctness_before_timing.k32_k64: v3-2 and v3-3 (crossover 1) on all 500 queries at 1M for k=32 and k=64, compared with oracles cut from the cpu_pilot top-100 oracle (the canonical order is total, so the top-k is the first k entries of the top-100); done as the first step of the Measurement A session.
correctness_before_timing.rule: any mismatch stops the session; the failing output is kept

gpu_policy.idle_check: before every process: no compute process on the GPU (nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps) and none of our scorer or profiler processes running (pgrep -f with bracketed patterns so the check does not match itself); otherwise wait in 30 s steps up to 30 minutes, then stop the session
gpu_policy.monitoring: for the whole session: nvidia-smi pmon -s um -d 1 and a 0.5 s poll of --query-compute-apps (pid, used memory) with UTC timestamps; every process records its own PID and UTC start/end
gpu_policy.overlap: a process overlaps if any GPU process not owned by our user is seen between its start and end (1 s margin on both sides, in either monitor). An overlapping process is preserved (its directory renamed with suffix -overlap-<n>, kept in the run and the manifest) and replaced: the same slot is rerun after the idle check. At most 3 replacements per slot; on the 4th overlap the session stops and is reported.
gpu_policy.redaction: logs record PIDs, owner class (ours/other), SM %, memory; process names, paths and other users' usernames are not recorded, and any that reach a committed file are replaced by <other-user>
gpu_policy.samplers: every sampler started by a session is killed at the end of the session, also on failure (trap)

measurement_A.name: paired timing at 1M
measurement_A.script: code/run_timing.sh (written and reviewed before the run)

workload.queries: data/derived/calibration-500.tsv, all 500; the 6,480 held-out queries are not used

measurement_A.order: rotating within each set: in round p (p = 0, 1, 2), implementation (i + offset_p) mod n runs i-th, offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
measurement_A.boundary: as V2-5: host query construction, kernel launch (query as kernel argument), result D2H, event synchronisation; index load, rank setup, validation and file writes excluded
measurement_A.during_timing: every saved top-k group of every warm-up and measured round is compared with the oracle after each process; any mismatch stops the session

analysis.reduction: per process, median wall latency of each query over the 20 measured rounds
analysis.statistic: geometric mean over queries of paired ratios (variant / reference, process p with process p of the same round), pooled over the 3 x 500 query/process pairs
analysis.uncertainty: crossed query/process bootstrap, 10,000 draws, 95% percentile interval, seed 20261117; conditional on this calibration set and session
analysis.also_reported: pooled median latency and median GPU event span per implementation and k; per-process medians
analysis.decision_language: a ratio is called faster/slower only when its 95% interval excludes 1; otherwise 'no difference resolved'
analysis.crossover_rule: recommended radix crossover = the smallest k in {32, 64, 100} at which v3-3/v3-2 has its upper 95% bound below 1; if none, keep 100 and report 'radix not shown faster at k <= 100'. k values below 32 are not tested, so 32 is the lowest possible recommendation. k=1000 has no v3-2 run; v3-3/ctrl there is reported but not part of the rule.

measurement_B.name: stage, barrier and host/GPU profile of ctrl and v3-all
measurement_B.script: code/run_profile.sh (written and reviewed before the run)
measurement_B.workload: 1M documents, W=1024, 256 threads, first 25 calibration queries, batch 1, k = 10 and k = 100 (v3-all uses its small-k path at k=10 and the radix path at k=100)

steps_per_k.reference: normal binaries of ctrl and v3-all, 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds, one process each: wall and event span per query, to relate profiled numbers to unprofiled ones
steps_per_k.clocks: clock builds (ctrl-instrumented and v3-all with -DRBP_STAGE_CLOCKS), RBP_CLOCKS_OUT, 3 warm-up + 5 measured rounds: stage table (setup, decode+add, local top-k, candidate write and done counter, merge tail; mean per block and critical path) and per-barrier-site table (wait mean, max and share for S1-S7) with analysis/analyze_clocks.py
steps_per_k.nsys: normal binaries under nsys profile --trace=cuda, 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds; per query host versus GPU time (GPU busy, span, launch call, launch-to-kernel latency, copy call and return) with analysis/analyze_nsys_v2.py from the SQLite export
steps_per_k.theta_counts: stats build of v3-all, RBP_V3_STATS_OUT, 1 warm-up + 5 measured rounds: per query candidates written by all ranges and survivors of the final filter (median, max); ctrl writes ranges x k by construction (977 x k)

measurement_B.order: for k=10 then k=100: reference (ctrl, v3-all), clocks (ctrl, v3-all), nsys (ctrl, v3-all), theta_counts (v3-all)
measurement_B.correctness: every step's saved top-k compared with the oracle before its numbers are used
limits: the new barriers of changes 2 and 3 (theta rank/read barriers; radix pass and bitonic barriers) carry no clock markers: their waits are inside the 'local top-k' and 'candidate write' stage times, not in the per-site table; sites S1-S7 keep their V2-5 meaning in both builds
clock and profiler numbers are diagnostic; latency claims come only from Measurement A

artifacts: small CSV/JSON exports and tables committed; .nsys-rep, SQLite exports, clock .bin dumps and raw CSV/TSV over 1 MB kept in run-bulk with SHA-256 via scripts/package_run.py
stopping: all correctness before timing; no optional stopping; a technical failure is inspected, fixed, reviewed and rerun under a new run ID, at most three attempts; overlap replacements follow gpu_policy.overlap
not_in_this_registration: the full collection; other range sizes; held-out queries; lookup chunk 8 (RBP_LOOKUP_CHUNK_WORDS=8) and 11-bit radix digits; Nsight Compute; any further code change. Each needs its own registration or an amendment before it runs.

questions.Q1: Is uniform radix close enough to the current small-k path at small k (k=10, 16) to keep one code path?
questions.Q2: Why is radix slower than ctrl at k=1000 at W=1024: the theta filter, radix, or both? Hypothesis: at W=1024 a range's 1,000th score is usually 0, so theta filters nothing, and radix sorts about 1,024 keys per range.
questions.Q3: Does W=4096 beat W=1024 at some k, with and without the v3 changes?

stats_set.per_query: candidates written, survivors after the final filter (GPU stats build); final theta and the share of ranges (with >= k documents) whose local k-th score is 0 (analysis/theta_cpu.cpp, exact CPU reference from the GSP index; ranges are uniform blocks of GSP order). The CPU survivors must equal the GPU survivors for every measured launch (checked against Measurement B's 300 rows before registration: 0 mismatches).
stats_set.summaries: median / IQR / max over queries of candidates written and survivors; share of queries with theta = 0; share of ranges with a zero k-th score (per-query median and pooled)

R1.rule: Uniform code. Per W, adopt v3-3r (theta + radix at every k, no branch on k) if v3-3r / v3-2 has its upper 95% bound <= 1.02 at BOTH k=10 and k=16. If not, report how far it misses, and give as fallback the crossover k = the smallest k in {16, 32, 100} with an upper bound < 1. Also report v3-3r / ctrl (same W) at k=1000 as the cost of uniformity at large k.

R2.rule: k=1000 attribution, per W: v3-2 / ctrl (cost of theta) and v3-3r / v3-2 (cost of radix). A factor whose upper 95% bound is > 1 is named as a cause.

R3.rule: W per k: report every (variant, W) cell's ratio to ctrl-w1024 and, per variant, W=4096 / W=1024. The best cell of each W is the one with the lowest point estimate of its ratio to ctrl-w1024 (ctrl-w1024 = 1). Recommend W=4096 for that k only if best W=4096 cell / best W=1024 cell has an upper 95% bound < 1; otherwise W=1024. Labelled calibration tuning, to be frozen before held-out evaluation.
